questions.q: What IS this feature in one sentence?
questions.a: Controls how MetaHuman NPCs perceive, collect, and offer biome-specific resources to the player based on their assigned biome.

questions.q: What wider system does it belong to?
questions.a: The biome_resources rung, which governs all resource availability, collection, and NPC interaction per biome zone.

questions.q: What would break if this feature didn't exist?
questions.a: MetaHuman NPCs would collect random resources regardless of their biome, breaking the fiction that an arctic NPC knows desert resources.

questions.q: What existing feature does this most resemble?
questions.a: npc_social — both define NPC behavior boundaries. This one specializes NPC resource knowledge by biome.

questions.q: Is this a rung, a sub-rung, or a parameter?
questions.a: Sub-rung auto-decomposed from biome_resources.

questions.q: What physical constraint does it encode?
questions.a: A MetaHuman can only offer resources native to its home biome. NPC in the methane lake biome cannot give you silicon wafer.

questions.q: What is the ONE measurement that proves it works?
questions.a: When queried for resource offers, an NPC's offer list contains 100% biome-native resources and 0% off-biome resources across 10+ biome types.

questions.q: What wall must it never violate?
questions.a: Must never prevent an NPC from offering a resource that was TRADED to them (player-gifted items bypass biome lock).

questions.q: What would a degenerate winner look like?
questions.a: An NPC that offers no resources (empty list) because the biome constraint matched zero catalog elements, or one that offers everything ignoring biome boundaries.

questions.q: How would we know if the constraint is too loose?
questions.a: If a desert NPC offers ice chunks, the biome constraint is not discriminating enough.

questions.q: At what scale does this feature operate?
questions.a: Per-NPC-instance, evaluated when player opens dialogue with a MetaHuman (every interaction, ~1-5/sec during social gameplay).

questions.q: What is the right definition level for this scale?
questions.a: Parameter-level: 3 variables (npc_home_biome, resource_offer_map, player_gift_overrides).

questions.q: Could this be decomposed further? Into what?
questions.a: Could split NPC resource offer frequency into per-biome-rate, but 3 parameters cover the essential constraint.

questions.q: At what resolution does the pattern emerge?
questions.a: Pattern emerges when the player talks to 3+ NPCs in different biomes and receives non-overlapping resource offers.

questions.q: What would 'deep enough' look like for this feature?
questions.a: When NPC resource offers form distinct clusters per biome with zero cross-biome contamination in the offer lists.

questions.q: What element catalog variables does this train?
questions.a: npc_home_biome_id, resource_offer_whitelist, player_gift_bypass_flag.

questions.q: How many relevant elements exist in the catalog?
questions.a: 38 catalog entries tagged 'metahuman' and 'npc' — enough to define biome-resource mappings.

questions.q: Are there enough variables to train meaningfully?
questions.a: Yes — 3 parameters with 38 catalog references provide sufficient constraint resolution.

questions.q: What variables are MISSING from the catalog?
questions.a: Per-NPC personality-bias that could override biome logic (e.g., a trader who travels between biomes).

questions.q: Would training this require GPU acceleration?
questions.a: No — 3 variables is far below the 1000-variable GPU threshold.

questions.q: Does this feature connect to the Mirror of Erised?
questions.a: Yes — the NPC's ability to give you the right biome resources IS the Mirror's give/receive loop. An NPC that offers nothing relevant cannot trigger the signal.

questions.q: How directly does it serve the Mirror? (direct/enabling/orthogonal)
questions.a: Direct — the give loop requires NPCs to have the right resources to offer.

questions.q: Would a costless life still be meaningful without this feature?
questions.a: No — if NPCs offer random resources, the player cannot give strategically and the Mirror loses its signal.

questions.q: Could this feature be gamed to fake a generous life?
questions.a: Partially — a player could memorize which biome has which NPC and exploit trade routes. But the resource scarcity itself prevents infinite loops.

questions.q: What would this feature look like if it perfectly served the Mirror?
questions.a: Every NPC is a living extension of their biome. The player walks up to a desert NPC and instinctively knows: 'they will have sand, salt, and glass.' The give loop is frictionless.

questions.q: What other features does this compose with?
questions.a: npc_social (dialogue context), biome_resources (parent), fabricator_economy (resource exchange values).

questions.q: What could break at the seam between this and its neighbors?
questions.a: If the NPC Social rung gives a dialogue line offering 'rare crystals' but the biome resource map says this biome has no rare crystals, the NPC lies to the player.

questions.q: Does this need a decoder step to place in the level?
questions.a: No — NPC resource mapping is data, not level geometry.

questions.q: What would a failed composition look like?
questions.a: Player gives a critically scarce resource to an NPC, but the NPC has nothing biome-native to offer back — deadlock.

questions.q: Does this feature need a human judgment or can the system verify it?
questions.a: System verifies biome-resource mapping alignment. Human judges whether the NPC feels like a genuine inhabitant of that biome.

questions.q: How many generations to converge?
questions.a: ~40 generations at pop=32 for 3-parameter mapping constraint.

questions.q: What population size is appropriate?
questions.a: 32 — small constraint space makes larger populations wasteful.

questions.q: What's the risk of overfitting?
questions.a: Low — the constraint is a hard mapping: one biome per NPC, one resource list per biome.

questions.q: What's the risk of underfitting?
questions.a: Low — a single mapping variable per NPC plus a list of allowed resources is exhaustive.

questions.q: Does the existing trainer support this domain type?
questions.a: Yes — core.trainer handles category-mapping constraints with catalog element whitelisting.

questions.q: Have we gone deep enough on this feature?
questions.a: Yes — 3 parameters with one hard mapping constraint is adequate for an NPC capability sub-rung.

questions.q: What would the NEXT level of decomposition look like?
questions.a: Per-NPC personality bias: one sub-sub-rung for each of the 3 MetaHuman archetypes (trader/settler/scavenger).

questions.q: If we stopped here, would the game feel complete?
questions.a: Yes — biome-locked NPC offers are a core mechanic. Missing it would be immediately noticeable.

questions.q: What is the human's expected emotional response to this feature?
questions.a: Trust — 'this NPC knows what this place has.' The biome consistency makes the world feel governed by rules the player can learn.

questions.q: Does this feature exist because the Mirror demands it, or because it's technically interesting?
questions.a: The Mirror demands it — biome-locked NPC offers are the material condition for meaningful giving.
